item.title: El Sayed's left-wing allies attack 'evil' Stevens after bombshell Rogers endorsement
item.description: Hasan Piker, Mehdi Hasan and others attacked Haley Stevens on X after she surprisingly endorsed Republican Mike Rogers in the heated Michigan Senate race.
item.content:encoded:
Left-wing allies of Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed erupted Sunday after the stunning decision by Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens to endorse his Republican rival Mike Rogers.

Stevens, who narrowly lost in the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, has been critical of his unwillingness to condemn the overt antisemitism of some of his supporters. After recent barbs between the two, El-Sayed disinvited her from a campaign event meant to showcase party unity in the critical Senate race, before she then endorsed his GOP opponent in a surprising last-second decision.

Far-left streamer Hasan Piker attacked her motives in a post to X, claiming she was "weirdly obsessed with Israel."

"haley stevens is not the spokesperson for democrats, she’s not the spox for jewish people or black people," Piker said on X. "she’s a self interested striver who’s weirdly obsessed with israel and has been paid handsomely for this strange obsession. this race is about solving the affordability crisis, defending democracy, fighting back against the racialized violence all communities have faced since trump came into power and serving michigan. haley and mike rogers serve trump, and trump serves the epstein class. the choice is clear."

DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS ENDORSES GOP SENATE NOMINEE MIKE ROGERS AT DETROIT CHURCH

"She’s clearly a disturbed, deranged, dishonest woman (less than 48 hours ago she was swearing to the NYT she was backing Abdul)," Zeteo News' editor-in-chief Mehdi Hasan also said on X, going on to attack the Democratic establishment for putting forward a "complete traitor."

In another post agreeing with Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen accusing Stevens of being used as a "tool" for "racism and religious bigotry," Hasan said "Islamophobia" was "at the core" of her endorsement.

Hasan also questioned Democratic leaders’ support for Stevens, writing, "She's evil."

Former DNC Vice Chair David Hogg also attacked Stevens and urged Democrats to denounce the congresswoman, who has said she remains a proud Democrat.

"If you supported Haley Stevens now is your time to speak out, denounce her as the Republican she is and apologize for supporting a traitor," Hogg wrote.

ABDUL EL-SAYED PLAYS DOWN HASAN PIKER TIES AFTER STREAMER’S VIRAL ANTISEMITISM FIRESTORM

The endorsement followed a controversial ad put up by Rebellion PAC, founded by The Young Turks host Cenk Uygur, in support of El-Sayed's campaign. The ad depicted grocery shoppers blaming U.S. military support for Israel for high grocery prices. Stevens called the ad antisemitic and demanded El-Sayed condemn it. His campaign said it was not affiliated with the ad, and he subsequently said he disagreed with its contents.

Uygur defended the Rebellion PAC's advertisement before the endorsement, disputing claims that it blamed Jewish people for grocery prices. He said the spot concerned Israel and accused reporters of misrepresenting the message.

On Sunday, Uygur claimed Stevens endorsed Rogers because "her only source of power is the Israeli lobby" and "She has no popular support, just AIPAC money." 

Former Obama aides and "Pod Save America" co-hosts Jon Lovett and Tommy Vietor also criticized Stevens for backing Rogers.

"So [Stevens] didn’t feel welcome at a political event, so now she doesn’t care if Democrats win the Senate," Lovett wrote. "She’s against ‘hate’ while supporting one of the most hateful campaigns in memory. She endorsed then unendorsed then endorsed then unendorsed her former rival, who she promised to unite behind, after endlessly repeating (correctly!) that Mike Rogers MUST be defeated. What an incoherent disgrace. Hope this anger drives people to do whatever they can to help [El-Sayed] win."

Vietor also wrote, "I hope folks will think about the fact that [Stevens] demanded that [El-Sayed] denounce as antisemitic an ad he was not associated with, but is now endorsing a man who called Abdul a terrorist. She is fine with bigotry and racism as long as its against the right people."

EL-SAYED DISTANCES HIMSELF FROM HASAN PIKER AFTER DISTURBING REMARKS ABOUT JEWISH AMERICANS

El-Sayed previously addressed the ad controversy, saying his campaign did not produce the Rebellion PAC advertisement and that he disagreed with its contents.

"You guys love to play the condemn game. I've already been clear that that ad was not made by me, and I do not agree with the contents of that ad," El-Sayed said in a campaign press gaggle Saturday.

The Republican National Committee welcomed Stevens’ decision. In a statement provided to Fox News Digital, RNC spokesman Hunter Lovell said the endorsement demonstrated Rogers’ appeal beyond Republican voters.

"When Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who ran against Abdul El-Sayed and knows him better than anyone, stands with Mike Rogers, Michigan should take notice," Lovell said. "Democrats who feel Abdul has abandoned them have a home with Mike, who is building a winning coalition of Democrats, Independents, and Republicans to save Michigan from El-Sayed's radical, terrorist-sympathizing agenda. The center of Michigan politics has moved, and Abdul is on the wrong side of it."

ROGERS WARNS MICHIGAN VOTERS AGAINST EL-SAYED’S ‘EXTREME’ AGENDA AHEAD OF ELECTION

Journalist Sam Robinson asked Stevenson Sunday how she could support a candidate whose positions directly opposed hers.

"Nothing is perfect," Stevens said.

The video shows a heckler interrupting Robinson, ending the exchange.

"Stevens is a traitor," the heckler said.

Stevens’ fiancé, Jason Turkish, and former campaign chairman David Kramer had already decided to vote for Rogers, Fox News Digital reported.

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Week 9 AP Top 25 Poll makes a mockery of Wake Forest and a laughable overreaction to USC's win over Buckeyes
item.description: Miami holds No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll at 8-0, but voters' treatment of Wake Forest and USC's massive 13-spot jump sparks serious debate.
item.content:encoded:
The first edition of the College Football Playoff rankings will be released on November 3, marking a point in the 2026 college football season when the AP Top 25 Poll takes a back seat, but that doesn't mean we're going to start ignoring the always-controversial poll. Someone has to keep tabs on the AP voters who can't possibly watch all these games and are forced to scramble and put together a list of the best 25 teams in the country.

With just two matchups featuring ranked opponents on the Week 8 slate, nobody was expecting too many fireworks, but the one boom we did get out in Los Angeles courtesy of USC, voters made sure to overreact.

On the other side of the country, Wake Forest moved to 7-1 and continued its run of absolutely throttling opponents, but apparently, outscoring your last two opponents 92-14 doesn't matter much.

Voters managed to put together the correct collection of the Top 5 teams in the country, but did so in the incorrect order. A shocking development, we know.

While Miami played with its food in Chapel Hill on Saturday, the Hurricanes improved to 8-0 and are the most-talented and most-explosive of the three unbeaten teams remaining, making the No. 1 next to their name completely justified.

THESE NUMBERS SHOW JUST HOW FRAUDULENT NOTRE DAME HAS BEEN DURING THE MARCUS FREEMAN ERA

Georgia did exactly what was expected of it by throttling Florida following a bye week after its inexplicable loss at home to Auburn. Then, you have Utah at No. 3, which is where we can officially start arguing, or at least begin nitpicking.

Utah is 8-0, but the Utes' 8-0 isn't as impressive as UCLA's 8-0. Utah has beaten exactly one team with a pulse, then No. 14 Houston at home, while the Bruins won on the road at then No. 13 Oregon. UCLA getting the nod for the three with Utah sliding to the four seems more sensible.

Notre Dame is a spot too high at No. 4. For starters, the Fighting Irish have lost a game unlike UCLA and Utah, and you could argue their most impressive win came in Week 1 on a neutral site against a now 5-3 Wisconsin team. Notre Dame getting a touch of bias is as inevitable as water remaining to be wet.

The Demon Deacons embarrassed Virginia 51-7 on Saturday to move to 7-1 on the year, with their lone loss being a 13-point defeat to No. 1 Miami. Despite having lost just once, putting together a 44-point win, and possessing an offense that has outscored opponents 187-31 over the last four weeks, Wake Forest did not budge in this week's poll.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Meanwhile, Kentucky and Alabama were both on byes this past weekend, but even they managed to move up one spot compared to last week.

The reality of the situation is that Wake Forest is being penalized by its own schedule and a laughably weak ACC. With how the dominoes are falling in the conference, Wake Forest could finish the season 11-1 with its most impressive win being a road victory at Purdue in Week 2.

Yes, even above-average teams are supposed to handle Stanford, NC State, Cal and Virginia, but the way in which Wake Forest has embarrassed all four of those down-and-out squads is more impressive than the No. 14 next to its name.

So, USC beats an Ohio State team without its starting quarterback and technically moves up THIRTEEN spots in the poll to No. 18? The same USC team that lost at Wisconsin a week ago, the same Badgers team that lost 30-0 to Iowa on Saturday? Is this the same USC team that was embarrassed at home by Oregon in Week 5 by two touchdowns?

This is your classic prisoner of the moment situation with an unranked team beating the No. 2 team in the country, but the asterisk that needs to go alongside that Buckeyes team the Trojans beat is a significant one.

AP voters missed out on doing something hilarious this week.

New Mexico improved to 7-1 on the year after going on the road and knocking off San Jose State on Halloween and kept a very weird streak alive.

The Lobos have scored exactly 21 points in each of their last three games, beating Hawaii 21-10, North Dakota State 21-16 and San Jose State by the same 21-16 score. New Mexico should be ranked No. 21, not No. 22, based on this scoring trend alone.

In all seriousness, Jason Eck's squad deserves some serious praise. The Lobos are 16-5 since Eck took over in 2025, which isn't bad considering the program hadn't been to a bowl game since 2016 prior to his arrival in Albuquerque.

item.title: Lincoln Riley has confrontation with Ohio State AD, reads prepared statement to media after huge USC win
item.description: The USC Trojans stunned the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes just days after a dismal loss to Wisconsin, capping a wild week for Lincoln Riley's program.
item.content:encoded:
What a wild week it's been for the USC Trojans.

Just last Saturday, it seemed like the Lincoln Riley era in Los Angeles was nearing its end. SC went into Madison as a sizable favorite over the Wisconsin Badgers and laid what can only be described as, charitably, an egg. For the first time in his coaching career, a Lincoln Riley team scored just seven points in a game.

There were head-scratching coaching mistakes, including attempting a 58-yard field goal against the wind. Predictably, it did not work, setting Wisconsin up with outstanding field position and a score. The Trojans looked poorly prepared and poorly coached, with senior quarterback Jayden Maiava taking multiple atrocious intentional grounding penalties and throwing two picks, a muffed catch on a Badgers kickoff leading to a missed opportunity before halftime, not calling timeout when the SC defense was misaligned on a pivotal fourth-and-2, leading to a Wisconsin touchdown, and an incredible -17 net rushing yards.

AFTER YET ANOTHER INEXCUSABLE LOSS TO WISCONSIN, THE LINCOLN RILEY ERA AT USC LOOKS TO BE NEARING AN END

After the game, the speculation and discussion was immediate. Riley was mentally checked out in LA, was one common sentiment. USC's athletic department had already started putting together funds to potentially clear Riley's rumored $70 million buyout. And fans and analysts were putting together wish lists of potential new coaches for 2027 and beyond.

Then, Saturday happened. USC hosted the Ohio State Buckeyes, still heavily favored despite starting backup quarterback Luke Fahey. OSU has a top three defense, arguably the best player in the country in Jeremiah Smith, and a wealth of big game experience under head coach Ryan Day. And sure enough, the Trojans dominated.

Even in a college football season where parity has been more obvious than ever, it was a shocking upset. Ohio State dominated time of possession and racked up yardage thanks to some garbage time drives, but never really looked like they had much of a chance. When set up with a first-and-goal inside the 1-yard-line, the Buckeyes still couldn't get in the end zone.

USC, which has been unimpressive for most of the season, looked like a totally different team. Star freshman Trent Mosley took a screen pass on the second play of the game for a long touchdown. Mark Bowman provided the highlight of the year from a tight end, hurdling an Ohio State defender and running through tackles on a huge catch and run. And the Trojans much-maligned defense grabbed an opportune turnover, forced a fumble that was inexplicably not reviewed, and got stop after stop when they needed it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Needless to say, a win over the number two team in the country was a season, and potentially program, altering turn of events. And Riley had a well, interesting, time after the conclusion, including a run-in with the Ohio State athletic director, and an unusual prepared statement that he read during postgame media availability.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Buckeyes staff and players were walking off the Coliseum field in the tunnel, and Riley tried to walk to the same area with his family and security guard. But an OSU staffer held him up, and after a few seconds, athletic director Ross Bjork can be seen gesturing back toward Riley and saying something toward him. Whatever it was, Riley was not happy about it, clearly saying some very profane phrases back as he was finally let through.

Another angle more clearly showed Bjork saying something indistinguishable as he left the field.

Confrontations happen, particularly after a heated game between two proud programs. Things got even a bit more unusual though, in the news conference.

LINCOLN RILEY ADDRESSES SPECULATION ABOUT HIS FUTURE AT USC AHEAD OF HUGE GAME AGAINST OHIO STATE

Riley, who already addressed speculation about his commitment to USC in a midweek news conference, saying LA is where he wants to be, read a prepared statement about his job and the Trojans program. This time, clearly with a bit more, shall we say, fesity language toward the media.

"This program is built on internal joy, not external applause," he said. "This win is for all the staff members, the players, the leaders, admin, all the people within the walls. I said before this game that I'm the right person for this job, and as long as all those people know that, that's all I care about. I appreciate being part of this university, and all it does. I appreciate our kids and our staff, and I'm going to continue to fight on because that's what being a Trojan is all about. Adios."

Not exactly what you'd expect to hear from a head coach coming off a huge win over the No. 2 ranked Ohio State Buckeyes, but it's hard to blame him for being a bit more defense than usual.

Riley's faced a long list of questions about his job status the past few weeks, but again, those questions are legitimate. USC's two losses this year were inexcusable. The Oregon Ducks are far from the team most expected in the preseason, and the Trojans defense let backup Dylan Raiola walk all over them in a 41-27 loss. That Wisconsin performance was dreadful, and looks even worse with the Badgers' 30-0 loss to Iowa on Saturday.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

There have been few signature wins in the Riley era, until this one, and after an offseason marketing campaign revolving around the "championship window" now being open, sitting at 6-2 with their season on the brink is simply not good enough. But he deserves credit for the OSU win and how it played out. USC looked like a different team; prepared, focused, intense, and aggressive. Why they don't always look like that? Nobody knows.

There are more questions moving forward though, because there always are. How do the Trojans, and Riley, respond in the final three games? The schedule doesn't get easier, with a trip to play the Indiana Hoosiers in Bloomington next week, and a date with the now-No. 5 UCLA Bruins at the Rose Bowl to close out the season.

Win out, and the Trojans would almost certainly be in the College Football Playoff, boasting one of the best resumes in the country with three wins over top-5 teams. Lose two of the last three to Indiana and UCLA and finish 8-4? We might be talking about Riley's buyout and that open job at Baylor all over again.
